findings.description: Multiple files with non-executable extensions (.cm, .osdi) contain PE/EXE/DLL binary signatures. The files are located in 'extension/ngspice/lib/ngspice/', which is not a standard path for ngspice configuration or model files.

The extension advertises itself as a circuit design tool using the 'ngspice' engine. While ngspice is a legitimate simulator, the presence of hidden PE binaries disguised as model files (.cm) is highly inconsistent with standard ngspice distribution. Legitimate ngspice model files are text-based SPICE netlists, not Windows executables. This suggests the 'ngspice' folder is a vector for delivering malware.

The extension reads the system clipboard via `vscode.env.clipboard.readText()` to support paste functionality in the custom editor. While this is a stated feature, combined with the presence of hidden executables, it raises the risk of credential or sensitive data exfiltration if the hidden binaries are executed or if the webview is compromised.
